# BigQuery answers for rings whose boundary touches a pole.
# The triangles are small to limit tessellation.

# The north pole is in the interior of the edge between -90 and 90 degrees longitude.
SELECT ST_ASGEOJSON(ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('POLYGON((-90 89.95, 90 89.95, 0 89.95, -90 89.95))'))

# The same boundary with the north pole explicitly present as a ring vertex.
SELECT ST_ASGEOJSON(ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('POLYGON((-90 89.95, 0 90, 90 89.95, 0 89.95, -90 89.95))'))
=> "{ \"type\": \"Polygon\", \"coordinates\": [ [ [0, 89.95], [3.81407567896023, 89.9530209480261], [8.13010388131908, 89.9558058246052], [12.9946187836019, 89.9583072974807], [18.4349510045835, 89.9604715262376], [24.4439568350634, 89.9622404777217], [30.9637581362363, 89.9635565465759], [37.8749845321538, 89.9643695135824], [45, 89.9646446564532], [52.1250154678463, 89.9643695135824], [59.0362418637637, 89.9635565465759], [65.5560431649366, 89.9622404777217], [71.5650489954165, 89.9604715262376], [77.0053812163981, 89.9583072974807], [81.8698961186809, 89.9558058246052], [86.1859243210398, 89.9530209480261], [90, 89.95], [89.999999999996, 89.975], [89.9999999999879, 89.9875], [89.9999999999719, 89.99375], [89.9999999999397, 89.996875], [89.9999999998754, 89.9984375], [89.9999999997467, 89.99921875], [89.9999999994894, 89.999609375], [89.9999999989748, 89.9998046875], [89.9999999989748, 90], [-89.9999999989748, 90], [-89.9999999989748, 89.9998046875], [-89.9999999994894, 89.999609375], [-89.9999999997467, 89.99921875], [-89.9999999998754, 89.9984375], [-89.9999999999397, 89.996875], [-89.9999999999719, 89.99375], [-89.9999999999879, 89.9875], [-89.999999999996, 89.975], [-90, 89.95], [-86.1859243210398, 89.9530209480261], [-81.8698961186809, 89.9558058246052], [-77.0053812163981, 89.9583072974807], [-71.5650489954165, 89.9604715262376], [-65.5560431649366, 89.9622404777217], [-59.0362418637637, 89.9635565465759], [-52.1250154678463, 89.9643695135824], [-45, 89.9646446564532], [-37.8749845321538, 89.9643695135824], [-30.9637581362363, 89.9635565465759], [-24.4439568350634, 89.9622404777217], [-18.4349510045835, 89.9604715262376], [-12.9946187836019, 89.9583072974807], [-8.13010388131908, 89.9558058246052], [-3.81407567896023, 89.9530209480261], [0, 89.95] ] ] } "

# A pole on the prime/antimeridian pair. The observed result is one closed
# ring meeting the pole at longitudes 0 and 180 (to the nearest degree).
WITH g AS (SELECT ST_ASGEOJSON(ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('POLYGON((0 89.95, 180 89.95, 90 89.95, 0 89.95))')) AS geojson),
  p AS (SELECT JSON_VALUE(geojson, '$.type') AS kind, JSON_QUERY_ARRAY(geojson, '$.coordinates') AS rings FROM g),
  r AS (SELECT kind, ARRAY_LENGTH(rings) AS ring_count, JSON_QUERY_ARRAY(rings[OFFSET(0)]) AS ring FROM p)
SELECT TO_JSON_STRING(STRUCT(kind, ring_count, ring[OFFSET(0)] = ARRAY_REVERSE(ring)[OFFSET(0)] AS closed, ARRAY(SELECT DISTINCT CAST(ROUND(CAST(JSON_VALUE(vertex, '$[0]') AS FLOAT64)) AS INT64) AS longitude FROM UNNEST(ring) AS vertex WHERE CAST(JSON_VALUE(vertex, '$[1]') AS FLOAT64) = 90 ORDER BY longitude) AS polar_longitudes)) FROM r
=> "{\"kind\":\"Polygon\",\"ring_count\":1,\"closed\":true,\"polar_longitudes\":[0,180]}"

# Rotating the north-pole triangle across the seam produces one closed ring
# on each side. Check the top edge of each ring independently of part order.
WITH g AS (SELECT ST_ASGEOJSON(ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('POLYGON((135 89.95, -45 89.95, -135 89.95, 135 89.95))')) AS geojson),
  p AS (SELECT JSON_VALUE(geojson, '$.type') AS kind, JSON_QUERY_ARRAY(poly, '$[0]') AS ring FROM g, UNNEST(JSON_QUERY_ARRAY(geojson, '$.coordinates')) AS poly),
  r AS (SELECT kind, ring[OFFSET(0)] = ARRAY_REVERSE(ring)[OFFSET(0)] AS closed, ARRAY(SELECT DISTINCT CAST(ROUND(CAST(JSON_VALUE(vertex, '$[0]') AS FLOAT64)) AS INT64) AS longitude FROM UNNEST(ring) AS vertex WHERE CAST(JSON_VALUE(vertex, '$[1]') AS FLOAT64) = 90 ORDER BY longitude) AS polar_longitudes FROM p)
SELECT TO_JSON_STRING(ARRAY_AGG(STRUCT(kind, closed, polar_longitudes) ORDER BY polar_longitudes[OFFSET(0)])) FROM r
=> "[{\"kind\":\"MultiPolygon\",\"closed\":true,\"polar_longitudes\":[-180,-45]},{\"kind\":\"MultiPolygon\",\"closed\":true,\"polar_longitudes\":[135,180]}]"

# An explicit vertex at the map corner still yields a single closed ring.
# BigQuery's intermediate vertices can be more than 10 m from the input edge,
# unlike the documented ST_ASGEOJSON tolerance in
# third_party/bigquery_docs/reference/standard-sql/geography_functions.md.
# The full observed output is retained in known_bugs.txt.
WITH g AS (SELECT ST_ASGEOJSON(ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('POLYGON((90 89.95, 180 90, -90 89.95, 0 89.95, 90 89.95))')) AS geojson),
  p AS (SELECT JSON_VALUE(geojson, '$.type') AS kind, JSON_QUERY_ARRAY(geojson, '$.coordinates') AS rings FROM g),
  r AS (SELECT kind, ARRAY_LENGTH(rings) AS ring_count, JSON_QUERY_ARRAY(rings[OFFSET(0)]) AS ring FROM p)
SELECT TO_JSON_STRING(STRUCT(kind, ring_count, ring[OFFSET(0)] = ARRAY_REVERSE(ring)[OFFSET(0)] AS closed)) FROM r
=> "{\"kind\":\"Polygon\",\"ring_count\":1,\"closed\":true}"

# The corresponding south-pole edge, with the ring traversed in reverse.
SELECT ST_ASGEOJSON(ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('POLYGON((90 -89.95, -90 -89.95, 0 -89.95, 90 -89.95))'))
